July 1 (Reuters) - Together AI on Wednesday said it has raised $800 million in a funding round led by Aramco ​Ventures [(2222.SE), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/2222.SE), more than doubling the artificial intelligence startup's ‌valuation to $8.3 billion.

Founded in 2022, the startup's platform lets companies train and run AI workloads on open models such as DeepSeek, ​MiniMax and Kimi at lower costs than closed ​systems.

- Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, Nvidia [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O), ⁠Salesforce Ventures [(CRM.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/CRM.N), March Capital, Pegatron and SentinelOne's [(S.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/S.N) S ​Ventures participated in the Series C round.

- Together AI was ​valued at [$3.3 billion](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/together-ai-notches-33-billion-valuation-after-latest-fundraising-2025-02-20/) in a February 2025 funding round led by General Catalyst, which had more than doubled its earlier [$1.25 billion](https://www.reuters.com/technology/together-ai-valued-125-bln-salesforce-led-funding-round-2024-03-13/) valuation from March ​2024.

- The company said it would use the Series ​C funding to widen its offerings as it expands into a ‌provider ⁠of inference, which is the process of running trained AI models.

- "The future of AI won't be owned by a few companies. It will be built by ​millions of ​developers and ⁠businesses, and open-source models are making that possible,” Together AI CEO Vipul Ved Prakash ​said.

- The AI startup's annual bookings crossed $1.15 billion ​last ⁠quarter on the back of rising open-source model usage, the company said. It counts firms such as Cursor, Cognition and Decagon among ⁠its ​customers.

- Together AI expects its computing ​capacity and infrastructure to expand roughly 50-fold over the next five years.


Reporting ​by Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda
